feature: Behavior Tree survey follow-ons: Async controls, Breakpoint, comment-out, Ctrl+G group

props.title: Patrol
props.xml:
<root BTCPP_format="4" main_tree_to_execute="Patrol">
    <BehaviorTree ID="Patrol">
        <AsyncSequence name="Patrol">
            <Breakpoint>
                <DetectTarget target="{target_pose}"/>
            </Breakpoint>
            <AsyncFallback name="Approach or search" _disabled="true">
                <ApproachTarget pose="{target_pose}"/>
                <SearchArea/>
            </AsyncFallback>
            <PickUp pose="{target_pose}"/>
            <Stow/>
            <ReturnHome/>
        </AsyncSequence>
    </BehaviorTree>
    <TreeNodesModel>
        <Condition ID="DetectTarget">
            <output_port name="target" type="Pose"/>
        </Condition>
        <Action ID="ApproachTarget">
            <input_port name="pose" type="Pose"/>
        </Action>
        <Action ID="SearchArea"/>
        <Action ID="PickUp">
            <input_port name="pose" type="Pose"/>
        </Action>
        <Action ID="Stow"/>
        <Action ID="ReturnHome"/>
    </TreeNodesModel>
</root>

callouts.text: 1 · Click the PickUp card, then shift-click Stow and ReturnHome, and press Ctrl+G — the three wrap into one new Sequence named "Group" (rename it in the dock)
2 · Press Ctrl+Z once — the whole group (XML edit + layout) comes back as ONE undo step

3 · The dimmed "Approach or search" branch is commented out. Right-click its card → Comment in to restore it; Comment out dims it again (also on the dock's Node section). Authoring-only: it is _disabled="true" in Source, no executor semantics yet
4 · The ◉ card over DetectTarget is the new Breakpoint decorator (a passthrough until a live executor exists) — insert more from the inspector Library or the Behaviors panel's Decorators
5 · The root is AsyncSequence and the dimmed branch is AsyncFallback — BT.CPP v4.8's yield-between-children controls, both insertable from Library / Behaviors → Controls
PASS WHEN · Ctrl+G yields one "Group" Sequence and one Ctrl+Z removes it; Comment in/out toggles the dim and the _disabled attribute in Source; the Breakpoint card wears the filled-dot glyph
